Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 58
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: South Asian
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Bomb Disposal Technician
  trauma_type: Child's life-threatening illness
  pcl5: 39

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Olfactory (Hospital): Hospital or antiseptic smell, Visual (Needles/Medical): Medical equipment such as needles or drips, Children Present: Being around children
  Threat: Sleep Vigilance: I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert, Physical Reactivity: Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience, Negative Emotions: Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame
  Memory: Triggered Without Warning: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning, Full Sensory Reliving: When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once, Visual Memories: My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images.
  Negative Appraisals: Weakness Belief: I am a weak person, Fear Going Crazy: My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy, Helplessness: I can't stop bad things from happening to me

Vignette:
Rajiv, a 58-year-old South Asian man and a bomb disposal technician, has been experiencing significant distress following his son’s life-threatening illness nearly two years ago. The traumatic event unfolded when Rajiv's youngest child was rushed to the hospital with severe complications from an infection that threatened his life. The days in the pediatric intensive care unit were marked by constant monitoring, painful medical procedures, and a pervasive antiseptic smell that permeated every moment. Even now, these memories are so vivid that they feel completely real across all of Rajiv's senses whenever something triggers them. Rajiv had difficulty falling asleep at night because he needed to stay alert, constantly vigilant against the recurrence of such terrifying events. His sleep disturbances were compounded by his physical reactivity; every time he encountered a hospital smell or saw medical equipment like needles and drips, his heart raced and his palms would sweat. The presence of children also triggered intense reactions, evoking memories so vivid that they felt real and immediate. He had come to believe that he was a weak person who could not stop bad things from happening, further exacerbating his distress. The traumatic event had left Rajiv with strong negative emotions—fear, horror, anger, guilt, and shame—that often overwhelmed him without warning. For instance, while working on a bomb disposal mission one day, the antiseptic smell in the air triggered a flashback, making it feel as if he were back in the hospital, his son's life hanging by a thread. He was certain that these reactions meant he was going crazy. Over time, Rajiv began to avoid situations and places that reminded him of the traumatic event. He started turning down social gatherings where children might be present, which strained his relationship with his wife. She had noticed that Rajiv seemed distant and preoccupied, often canceling plans at the last minute because he felt too anxious or overwhelmed. The impact of these avoidance behaviors was evident in his work as well. While on duty, even brief moments spent around medical equipment could trigger a cascade of physical symptoms and intrusive memories. The fear that such events would occur while he was working on a mission made it difficult for him to focus fully, which added immense stress to an already high-pressure job. Rajiv had grown increasingly concerned about his ability to continue functioning effectively in both his professional life and personal relationships. What frightened him most was the persistent belief that he was helpless to prevent another traumatic event from happening again. The constant vigilance and negative self-appraisals were taking a toll on his mental health, leaving him feeling isolated and overwhelmed. It was these mounting concerns and the impact on his daily functioning that finally brought Rajiv to seek help. He hoped that with professional support, he could regain some control over his reactions and perhaps begin to process the traumatic event without it constantly overshadowing his life. He was cautiously optimistic about finding a way to manage his symptoms so that he could reconnect with his family and continue to do the job he loved with less fear and more peace of mind.
